subject: GlyphTech dedicated pool saturation — action plan & timeline
content:
From: Ops Team <ops@glyphtech.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 06 Nov 2028 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: High tail latency from reserved GPU pool - experiencing throttling

Hi Lukas / Marissa,

We started seeing sustained tail latency on our reserved GPU pool (GT-prod-dedicated) around 17:40 UTC. Requests that normally finish in ~120ms are spiking above 3s intermittently, and last 30 minutes show a steady increase in queue depth. This began right after a larger batch of long-context jobs (~8k tokens) hit the pool.

Attached is a trimmed service log and a short profile of the request distribution. Can you confirm whether any autoscale or eviction policy was triggered on your side? We need an ETA for mitigation — this is impacting our interactive feature.

Attachments: glyphtech_service_log_2028-11-06.txt (6KB)

— Sara Liu
Ops, GlyphTech

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops@glyphtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Nov 2028 19:05:23 +0000
Subject: Re: High tail latency from reserved GPU pool - experiencing throttling

Sara — thanks for the quick heads-up and the log. We see the same signal on our telemetry: a series of long-sequence requests caused KV-cache pressure and led to increased scheduling latency in that tenant's reserved pool.

Immediate actions we are taking now (short-term):
- Throttle large-context job ingress for your pool for the next 30 minutes (suppressing new >6k token requests).
- Increase worker concurrency soft-limits to shed some queued requests to spare headroom.
- Kick off a canary of a slightly modified batching policy targeted to the GT pool to reduce per-token scheduling overhead.

Ben is running the canary plan. We will post a live update in the Jira (OPS-1429) and share a customer-facing blurb in the next hour. Rough ETA for stabilization: 45–90 minutes.

— Lukas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Nov 2028 02:45:05 +0000
Subject: Re: High tail latency from reserved GPU pool - experiencing throttling

Quick technical summary and proposal:

Root hypothesis:
- The long-context batch pattern is causing KV cache churn and forcing frequent cross-worker cache fetches. That increases head-of-line blocking when combined with our default continuous batching window for that pool.

Proposed short-term canary config (attached): proposed_canary_config.yaml —
- Reduce continuous batching window from 30ms -> 10ms for GT-prod-dedicated.
- Enable lightweight prefix caching for sequences >2k tokens to avoid repeated KV reads.
- Limit concurrent long-context jobs per tenant to 3 (soft throttle).

Plan:
1) Roll canary in dev -> staging (10:05 UTC) — smoke tests.
2) If stable, roll to 25% of GT pool (10:25 UTC).
3) Full roll (11:00 UTC) and monitor 30m.

Risks/notes: warmup of prefix cache will add some initial latency for first requests but should reduce tail latency quickly. If we see no improvement in 30m after full roll, plan B is to temporarily burst GT to spare dedicated nodes for 2 hours (customerscope capacity bridging).

Attaching proposed_canary_config.yaml. I also created OPS-1429 and linked the drive folder with logs.

— Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 08 Nov 2028 14:20:12 +0000
Subject: Draft — Customer action plan and credit offer for GlyphTech (please review)

Sara, Lukas —

Thanks again for your patience. Below is the draft customer-facing action plan we propose sending after we confirm stabilization. Please review edits inline; I want to ensure we accurately capture the impact and the remediation timeline.

Customer-facing action plan (draft):
- Summary: On 2028-11-06 we observed sustained tail latency in GlyphTech's reserved pool caused by a pattern of long-context requests which led to cross-worker KV cache pressure.
- What we did: Rapid ingress throttling, canary of reduced batching window, enabled prefix caching for long sequences, and temporary concurrent-job limits.
- Results: Initial canary (rolled to 25%) reduced 95th percentile latency from ~1.6s to ~210ms within 20 minutes; full roll completed at 11:03 UTC on 2028-11-07 and metrics stabilized.
- Remediation & follow-up: We will create a permanent workload profile for GT that applies the above config, add a guard to prevent sudden bursts of >6k token jobs without a scheduled window, and schedule a joint runbook review session.
- Credits: We propose a one-month service credit on your Dedicated pool for the incident window.
- Timeline: Joint runbook review by 2028-11-16; postmortem published by 2028-11-23.

Attachments: customer_action_plan_draft.docx (1 page)

Marissa — can you confirm the credit amount and the dates? Also flag any legal/finance reviews needed.

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Stabilization confirmed and next steps — GlyphTech dedicated pool incident

Sara / Ops —

Stabilization confirmed. Summary of outcomes and next steps: 

1) Stabilization: The canary successfully reduced 95th percentile latency to ~200ms for the GT pool. Full roll completed 2028-11-07 11:03 UTC.
2) Permanent changes: We will ship the workload profile that includes the reduced batching window and prefix caching as a permanent guard for GT by 2028-11-14. This will be enforced at the routing layer (automated, not manual).
3) Automated guard: We will implement an ingestion guard that caps long-context job admission per tenant and raises a preemptive alert before autoscale triggers. Expected delivery: 2028-11-14.
4) Customer credit: We are prepared to apply a 45-day service credit to your next invoice per your request; I'll loop in billing and confirm the exact credit amount tomorrow.
5) Postmortem: Detailed postmortem and metrics will be published on 2028-11-23. We will schedule the joint runbook review for 2028-11-16; Marissa will send a calendar invite.

Apologies for the disruption; appreciate the GlyphTech ops team's collaboration on verification steps. If anything regresses, flag OPS-1429 and ping me directly — I will be on-call this weekend for post-deploy verification.

Regards,

Lukas Meyer
